masteryZone.q: A passenger in a bus is thrown forward when the bus suddenly stops. Which law explains this?
masteryZone.sol: Newton's First Law (Law of Inertia) — the passenger's body continues moving forward due to inertia even after the bus stops.

masteryZone.q: What is the SI unit of Force?
masteryZone.sol: Newton (N) is the SI unit of force. 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

masteryZone.q: True or False: Newton's first law is also called the Law of Acceleration.
masteryZone.sol: False. Newton's first law is the Law of Inertia. The second law (F = ma) is the Law of Acceleration.

masteryZone.q: When a bullet is fired from a gun, the gun recoils backward. This is an example of:
masteryZone.sol: Newton's Third Law — the gun exerts forward force on bullet (action), bullet exerts equal backward force on gun (reaction), causing recoil.

masteryZone.q: Which force is responsible for the motion of planets around the Sun?
masteryZone.sol: Gravitational force between the Sun and planets provides the necessary centripetal force for orbital motion.

masteryZone.q: Which of the following is NOT a contact force?
masteryZone.sol: Gravitational force is a non-contact (field) force. Friction, normal reaction, and tension require physical contact between objects.

masteryZone.q: What is the formula for centripetal force?
masteryZone.sol: Centripetal force F = mv²/r, where m = mass, v = velocity, r = radius of circular path.

masteryZone.q: What is the SI unit of force?
masteryZone.sol: Newton (N). 1 N = 1 kg·m/s².

masteryZone.q: Which type of friction has the LARGEST magnitude?
masteryZone.sol: Static friction is the strongest — it must overcome interlocking of surface irregularities to start motion.

masteryZone.q: Which type of friction has the SMALLEST magnitude?
masteryZone.sol: Rolling friction is the smallest. This is why wheels and ball bearings are used to reduce friction.

masteryZone.q: True or False: The coefficient of friction depends on the area of contact between surfaces.
masteryZone.sol: False. The coefficient of friction depends only on the nature (material and roughness) of the surfaces, NOT on the area of contact.

masteryZone.q: True or False: Lubrication reduces friction by creating a thin layer between surfaces.
masteryZone.sol: True. Oils and greases create a thin film that separates surfaces, converting dry friction into fluid friction which is much smaller.

masteryZone.q: The value of acceleration due to gravity (g) at Earth's surface is approximately:
masteryZone.sol: Standard value of g at Earth's surface = 9.8 m/s².

masteryZone.q: What happens to the value of 'g' as we go above the Earth's surface?
masteryZone.sol: g decreases with altitude: g' = g(1 - 2h/R) where h = height above surface and R = Earth's radius.

masteryZone.q: The value of g at the center of Earth is:
masteryZone.sol: At Earth's center, depth d = R, so g' = g(1 - R/R) = 0 m/s².

masteryZone.q: Escape velocity of Earth is approximately:
masteryZone.sol: Escape velocity ve = √(2gR) ≈ 11.2 km/s — minimum speed needed to overcome Earth's gravity.

masteryZone.q: Which equation relates final velocity (v), initial velocity (u), acceleration (a), and time (t)?
masteryZone.sol: v = u + at — the first equation of motion for constant acceleration.

masteryZone.q: In an elastic collision, which of the following is conserved?
masteryZone.sol: In elastic collisions, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved. In inelastic collisions, only momentum is conserved.

masteryZone.q: If the mass of a body is doubled and velocity is halved, momentum becomes:
masteryZone.sol: p = m × v. New p = (2m) × (v/2) = mv = same. Momentum remains unchanged.

masteryZone.q: True or False: According to the law of conservation of linear momentum, the total momentum of an isolated system remains constant if no external force acts.
masteryZone.sol: True. In the absence of external forces, total linear momentum is always conserved.
